title: Visual Cycle — DOMiNANCE Originals
source: KNUST Visual Cycle lecture (Edwin F. Laing) and accompanying study guide

questions.stem: Which retinal photoreceptors primarily support vision in dim light?
questions.why: Rods have high sensitivity and mediate scotopic vision.

questions.stem: Which photoreceptors chiefly permit discrimination of colours in bright light?
questions.why: Cones have distinct spectrally tuned opsins and mediate photopic colour vision.

questions.stem: Early night blindness with loss of peripheral vision suggests preferential injury to which cells?
questions.why: Rods are especially important for dim-light and peripheral visual sensitivity.

questions.stem: Which dietary substance serves as a plant-derived precursor of vitamin A?
questions.why: Beta-carotene can be cleaved to retinal and provides provitamin A activity.

questions.stem: Which dietary source supplies mainly preformed vitamin A rather than provitamin A carotenoids?
questions.why: Animal liver and liver oils supply preformed retinoids; vegetables generally contribute provitamin carotenoids.

questions.stem: What chemical group distinguishes retinal from retinol?
questions.why: Retinal is the aldehyde corresponding to the alcohol retinol.

questions.stem: Why can the 11-cis-retinal chromophore respond strongly to visible photons?
questions.why: The conjugated double-bond system absorbs light and permits photoisomerisation.

questions.stem: Which molecular transformation initiates the light response of rhodopsin?
questions.why: Absorption of light isomerises 11-cis-retinal to all-trans-retinal.

questions.stem: Which component supplies rhodopsin with its light-absorbing chromophore?
questions.why: Rhodopsin combines opsin with covalently attached 11-cis-retinal.

questions.stem: Which linkage attaches the retinal aldehyde to an opsin lysine residue?
questions.why: The retinal aldehyde condenses with the epsilon-amino group of a lysine to form a protonated Schiff base.

questions.stem: What explains the difference in light absorption between free retinal and intact rhodopsin?
questions.why: The protein binding pocket and Schiff-base protonation shift the chromophore absorption spectrum.

questions.stem: Which approximate wavelength is the absorption maximum of intact rhodopsin?
questions.why: The KNUST lecture lists the intact rhodopsin absorption maximum near 500 nm.

questions.stem: Why does vitamin A deficiency commonly cause early night blindness?
questions.why: Retinal is needed to regenerate rhodopsin, and rods are essential for dark vision.

questions.stem: Which photolytic rhodopsin intermediate can activate transducin?
questions.why: Metarhodopsin II is the active receptor state designated R*.

questions.stem: Why is a rod membrane relatively depolarised in the dark?
questions.why: Dark-state cGMP-gated cation channels permit the inward dark current.

questions.stem: How does illumination typically change the membrane potential of a rod photoreceptor?

options.label: B
options.text: It initiates a sodium action potential

questions.why: Light closes the cGMP-gated inward current, making the membrane potential more negative.

questions.stem: After rhodopsin activation, what happens to guanine nucleotide bound to transducin alpha?
questions.why: R* promotes GDP release and GTP binding on the heterotrimeric G protein transducin.

questions.stem: Which enzyme is activated by GTP-bound transducin alpha?
questions.why: Activated transducin stimulates PDE to hydrolyse cGMP.

questions.stem: What event directly closes cyclic nucleotide-gated channels following a flash of light?
questions.why: Phototransduction activates cGMP phosphodiesterase; the fall in cGMP closes the cation channels.

questions.stem: How does light generally alter glutamate release from rod synapses?
questions.why: Hyperpolarisation lowers presynaptic calcium entry and reduces tonic glutamate secretion.

questions.stem: Blocking transducin activation while leaving retinal photoisomerisation intact would chiefly prevent what?
questions.why: Transducin is required to activate PDE and produce the pronounced fall in cytosolic cGMP.

questions.stem: Which enzyme begins the shut-off of light-activated rhodopsin by phosphorylating it?
questions.why: Rhodopsin kinase phosphorylates active rhodopsin on serine/threonine residues.

questions.stem: What is the function of arrestin binding phosphorylated rhodopsin?
questions.why: Arrestin blocks further interaction between activated rhodopsin and transducin.

questions.stem: What is the intrinsic transducin reaction that helps terminate the light signal?
questions.why: The transducin alpha subunit hydrolyses its bound GTP and switches off PDE stimulation.

questions.stem: Which enzyme restores cGMP levels so that dark-current channels can reopen?
questions.why: Guanylate cyclase synthesises cGMP from GTP during recovery.

questions.stem: Why does the calcium concentration inside illuminated rod outer segments fall?

options.label: A
options.text: Calcium export stops while entry continues

options.label: B
options.text: Calcium is consumed to generate cGMP

options.label: C
options.text: Calcium entry falls while extrusion continues

options.label: D
options.text: Calcium becomes bound permanently to opsin

options.label: E
options.text: Calcium is converted enzymatically to sodium

questions.why: Closure of the cGMP-gated channels blocks influx while the exchanger continues calcium extrusion.

questions.stem: How does falling cytosolic calcium assist recovery after a light response?

options.label: B
options.text: It locks transducin in its active state

options.label: D
options.text: It blocks all guanylate cyclase activity

questions.why: Calcium-dependent feedback enhances guanylate cyclase activity, helping regenerate cGMP.

questions.stem: Which ion transport mechanism normally extrudes calcium from rod outer segments?
questions.why: An exchanger couples sodium entry and potassium movement to calcium extrusion.

questions.stem: Why is dark adaptation delayed when visual-pigment regeneration is impaired?

options.label: A
options.text: All cones must regenerate into rods

options.label: E
options.text: Synaptic glutamate stores are permanently lost

questions.why: Restoring high rod sensitivity depends on replenishing 11-cis-retinal-bound rhodopsin.

questions.stem: What produces different spectral sensitivities among the three classes of cone pigment?
questions.why: Cones use the same 11-cis-retinal chromophore but different opsins tune their wavelength sensitivity.

questions.stem: Which approximate wavelength corresponds to the lecture's blue cone absorption maximum?
questions.why: The lecture lists approximate blue, green and red cone maxima at 455, 530 and 625 nm.

questions.stem: A person lacks a working green-sensitive cone pigment. Which molecular defect is most likely?
questions.why: Red–green colour defects arise from absent or spectrally altered cone pigments.

questions.stem: Why are common red-green colour vision disorders more frequent in males?

options.label: A
options.text: All relevant cone opsin genes are Y-linked

options.label: B
options.text: Many cone opsin genes are X-linked

options.label: D
options.text: The trait requires paternal mitochondrial DNA

options.label: E
options.text: All cone signals depend on testosterone

questions.why: The red and green cone opsin genes lie on the X chromosome, making recessive defects more evident in males.
